questions.question: Who is responsible for operating a vehicle safely?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for safe vehicle operation. Always check your vehicle before driving a commercial motor vehicle.

questions.question: When driving, you should:

options.text: Avoid using your mirrors in heavy traffic.
Look only ahead and to the right.
Look ahead, to the sides, and behind your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead, to the sides, and behind your vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must know what is happening around your vehicle at all times. Check your mirrors regularly and scan the road ahead while driving.

questions.question: When backing a trailer:

options.text: You should not back in a straight line.
You should not fix drift until you are far off course.
You should move forward to reposition as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should move forward to reposition as needed.
questions.explanation: When backing a trailer, move forward to reposition your vehicle as needed.

questions.question: Night driving is:

options.text: Just as safe as day driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than day driving.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. You cannot see hazards as well. Headlight glare can reduce your vision. There are more tired and impaired drivers on the road at night.

questions.question: If you stay in neutral too long while changing gears:

options.text: You may have trouble shifting to the next gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have trouble shifting to the next gear.
questions.explanation: If you stay in neutral too long while changing gears, you may have trouble shifting to the next gear. If this happens, do not force the shift. Return to neutral, release the clutch, increase engine speed to match road speed, and try again.

questions.question: What is axle weight?

options.text: The weight an axle puts on the ground
The weight of the axle itself
How much weight an axle can carry

questions.correctAnswerText: The weight an axle puts on the ground
questions.explanation: Axle weight is the weight that one axle or set of axles puts on the ground.

questions.question: A jogger wearing headphones:

options.text: Probably knows what is happening around them.
May not know what is happening around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not know what is happening around them.
questions.explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists wearing headphones. They may not hear your vehicle coming and could do something dangerous because they do not know you are there.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a distracted person that concerns motorists?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger
A person sitting on a bench waiting for the bus
A construction worker on the roadside

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for the bus
questions.explanation: Be cautious around distracted people. Drivers and pedestrians talking to someone may not pay full attention to the road. Workers on or near the road may focus on their work and not watch traffic. They can also distract drivers.

questions.question: When checking power steering hoses before driving, look for:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leaks
questions.explanation: Check the power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid level before driving. Look especially for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: Hanging meat:

options.text: Should never be transported by trailer
Must be approved by the EPA

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be an unstable load
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is an unstable load. It has a high center of gravity. The swinging meat can affect how you handle the vehicle. Drive carefully with this cargo.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Allow the rear wheels to lock up
Allow all wheels to lock up
Alert other drivers when you are braking

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop wheels from locking up
questions.explanation: ABS prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: What affects how far your vehicle travels before stopping?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed
questions.explanation: Stopping distance is affected by your speed, your vehicle's weight, and how slippery the road surface is.

questions.question: How should you brake if your vehicle's ABS is not working?

options.text: Brake normally. Your regular brakes still work.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally. Your regular brakes still work.
questions.explanation: Without ABS, your vehicle still has normal brakes. Drive and brake as usual. Have your ABS fixed as soon as possible.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about ____ to your stopping distance.
questions.correctAnswerText: 32 feet
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your stopping distance.

questions.question: When you push the brake pedal, air brakes work:

options.text: Only if it is warm outside

questions.correctAnswerText: After a short delay
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the lines to the brakes. There is a delay of at least half a second between when you press the brake pedal and when the brakes start working.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that moves air from the compressor to the tanks
A noise made by air brakes when used
A part in the braking unit that lets air move freely

questions.correctAnswerText: A warning system
questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into your view when air pressure drops below 60 psi.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Mechanical
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: service brake, parking brake, and emergency brake. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: What must you do before transporting a load that is too long?

options.text: Get special permits from the Department of Transportation
Alert the fire departments along your route

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits from the Department of Transportation
questions.explanation: Loads that are too long, too wide, or too heavy need special permits from the Department of Transportation.

questions.question: If you are unsure your vehicle will fit under a bridge, you should:

options.text: Swerve as you pass under the bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will safely pass under an overhead object, slow down and find another route if possible.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Complete the test without a moving violation
Obey traffic signs and signals only if other traffic is present

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey traffic signs and signals only if other traffic is present
questions.explanation: You must drive safely during the on-road test. This means wearing your safety belt, obeying all traffic signs and signals at all times, following all traffic laws, and avoiding accidents or moving violations.

questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is not a concern if no passengers are getting off.
Should not be on the road.
Is always a concern, whether you see passengers or not.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is always a concern, whether you see passengers or not.
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully around a stopped bus. Passengers may cross in front of or behind it. The bus may block their view of your vehicle.

questions.question: If you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test, you will:

options.text: Automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
Lose extra points from your score.

questions.correctAnswerText: Automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact with it at all times. If driving a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly means you automatically fail the test.

questions.question: What is the danger if your vehicle rolls backward when you start to accelerate?

options.text: You may hit a vehicle behind you.
You may lose your place in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit a vehicle behind you.
questions.explanation: Keep your vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop to avoid hitting something behind you. If your vehicle has a manual transmission, partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake.

questions.question: When driving, hold the steering wheel:

options.text: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
With both hands at the bottom of the wheel.
With both hands at the top of the wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands. Place them on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT show bad brakes?

options.text: Pads with no oil or grease on them

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads with no oil or grease on them
questions.explanation: When checking your brakes, look for cracked drums, shoes or pads covered in oil or grease, and shoes that are worn, broken, or dangerously thin. Clean pads without oil or grease are a sign of good brakes.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver has their high beam headlights on, you should:

options.text: Flash your high beams to tell them to turn theirs off.
Look toward the right side of your lane until the vehicle passes.
Pull over until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of your lane until the vehicle passes.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming vehicle uses high beams, look away from the lights toward the right side of the road until it passes. This stops the bright lights from blinding you.

questions.question: Front tire tread depth in the main grooves must be at least:
questions.correctAnswerText: 4/32 of an inch.
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread in every main groove. Other tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: While driving, ____ keeps spring brakes from engaging.
questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure
questions.explanation: Air pressure holds spring brakes in place while driving. If air pressure drops too low, the springs will activate the brakes automatically.

questions.question: To best reduce cell phone distractions while driving, you should:

options.text: Stay on one call for the entire trip.
Turn the phone off before driving.
Only use the phone for incoming calls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the phone off before driving.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid cell phone distractions is to turn your phone off before you start driving and leave it off until you reach your destination.

questions.question: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back up to the right.
Pull straight forward, then back up to the left.
Pull forward to the right, then back straight.
Pull forward to the left, then back straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back up to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, pull straight forward first, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must end up completely inside the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: During a trip, gauges help you:

options.text: Are the only way to find vehicle problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you spot vehicle problems.
questions.explanation: During a trip, check the gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights for problems.

questions.question: When stopped on the side of the road, a driver should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. This is very important at night.

questions.question: The suspension system:

options.text: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
Keeps the load at a safe distance behind the driver.
Keeps a safe distance between vehicles.
Makes the load lighter for the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. A broken suspension is very dangerous.

questions.question: A trailer brake hand valve can be used to:

options.text: Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: A trailer brake hand valve stops the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.question: Skids from acceleration are usually fixed by:

options.text: Lifting your foot off the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lifting your foot off the accelerator.
questions.explanation: Acceleration skids happen on slippery roads. Lift your foot off the accelerator to fix them.

questions.question: Heavy steering often means:
questions.correctAnswerText: A front tire has failed.
questions.explanation: Heavy steering usually means a front tire has failed. If your steering feels different, safely exit the road and check your tires.

questions.question: What is the only way to sober up after drinking?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for time to pass.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Cold showers and coffee do not speed this up. Time is the only way to sober up.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal down.
questions.explanation: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, push the brake pedal down. The harder you push, the more air pressure is released.

questions.question: How much water on a road causes hydroplaning?
questions.correctAnswerText: A small amount
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose grip on the road and slide on water. Only a small amount of water is needed.

questions.question: An after-trip inspection should be done:
questions.correctAnswerText: After every trip.
questions.explanation: Always inspect your vehicle at the end of each trip. Fill out a vehicle inspection report if required.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you that you plan to slow down?

options.text: Tap the brakes a few times before slowing down.
Turn on one set of turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap the brakes a few times before slowing down.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights. This warns drivers behind you that you are about to slow down.

questions.question: When is a vehicle inspection required?
questions.correctAnswerText: By state and federal law.
questions.explanation: State and federal laws require that commercial vehicle drivers inspect their vehicles before every trip.

questions.question: What happens when there is more alcohol in your body?

options.text: Your liver will digest the alcohol faster.
The alcohol will have less effect on you.
It will take longer for your body to remove the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will take longer for your body to remove the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Your body removes alcohol at a fixed rate. The more alcohol you drink, the longer it takes your body to remove it from your system.

questions.question: What should you do with engine belts during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Inspect them only if they look frayed.
Leave them alone and do not inspect them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them for tightness.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check all engine belts for tightness and wear.

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: A single air brake system that uses two sets of controls.
One air brake system for each side of the truck.
Two separate air brake systems that use a single set of controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate air brake systems that use a single set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems controlled by one set of brake controls. One system usually operates the brakes on the rear axle. The other system operates the brakes on the front axle.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
It turns on the air compressor.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the compressor pumps air into the storage tanks. It stops pumping if pressure gets too high and starts pumping if pressure gets too low.

questions.question: Why should you accelerate slowly on surfaces with poor traction?

options.text: Because it is always good to accelerate slowly.
To keep from losing control of the vehicle.
So you do not go faster than the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep from losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly in poor-traction conditions, such as rain or snow, to avoid losing control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do before backing up?

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to finish quickly.
Get out of the cab and walk your path to check for obstacles.
Use only the passenger side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the cab and walk your path to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, exit the cab and check your path for obstacles. Back up slowly and check both mirrors.

questions.question: When making a left turn with two available turn lanes, why should you start in the rightmost lane?

options.text: You can see other turning vehicles on your left better than on your right.
The vehicle will turn more quickly.
Other vehicles will get out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see other turning vehicles on your left better than on your right.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles must swing right to make left turns. Starting in the rightmost lane allows you to see other turning vehicles on your left instead of your right. This gives you a better view and reduces the risk of a collision.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle is hydroplaning?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel as hard as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane, do not use the brakes. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch. This will slow your vehicle and help it regain traction.
